editorial:
Imagine waking up in Madrid to find a killer who treats the city like a giant art gallery. You will follow a detective who has to track down a murderer targeting rich art collectors. The twist is that the killer isn't just killing people; he is posing the bodies to look exactly like the weird and creepy drawings from Goya's Los Caprichos series. It feels like a dark game of cat and mouse where the killer is always one step ahead, leaving a trail of artistic clues that make you feel uneasy but curious to see what happens next.

You will really appreciate the acting and the way the movie builds tension without relying on too many jump scares. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the reveal at the end makes the wait worth it. If you enjoy mysteries that mix high art with gritty crime, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when you discover the killer is actually someone close to the investigation. He wanted to punish people who bought art just for money rather than loving the craft. In the final showdown, the detective catches him just in time. The killer tries to complete one last scene, but he is stopped before he can finish his masterpiece. It ends with the detective finally finding peace after solving the puzzle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves detective stories and art mysteries.
